A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MEs are associated with activation of a common neural circuit that includes the medial prefrontals, and that self-evaluative MEs recruit the right dorsolateral PFC.
the right PFC is a region of the brain that is involved in the processing of ME, and that this involvement is modulated by the degree of self-relevance in the task.

the right PFC may be involved in the processing of self-relevant information, and this finding may have important implications for our understanding of the neural underpinnings of the self.
the right PFC may serve as the neural substrate for the metacognitive evaluation of self-relevant information.
